name: Oscillatory Coupling
description: Synchronization of neural oscillations across brain regions to enable binding, communication, and selective attention. Proposed mechanisms for feature integration, attentional gating, and long-range communication across cortical hierarchies.
key_references: Fries, P. (2015). Rhythms for cognition: communication through coherence. Neuron, 88(1), 220-235.
Singer, W., & Gray, C. M. (1995). Visual feature integration and the temporal correlation hypothesis. Annual Review of Neuroscience, 18, 555-586.
empirical_evidence: LFP and single-unit recordings showing coherence between areas during attention and binding tasks. Gamma-band (30-100 Hz) coherence increases when attention is directed to a stimulus. Alpha (8-12 Hz) oscillations modulate sensory gain. Theta rhythms in hippocampus correlate with memory formation.

parameters.frequency_bands: alpha: 8-12 Hz, beta: 15-30 Hz, gamma: 30-100 Hz
parameters.phase_lag_tolerance: varies by region pair and frequency
